description: Finds the fixtures whose GDTF profile matches a DMX channel list and the matched DMX mode: channel names in DMX order from address 1 (English, Czech, German or Spanish; abbreviations, synonyms and typos are understood), as in a manual, on a console or in a fixture-profile TXT. Give channels (a list) or text (a pasted list, or a TXT with one or more modes; rows such as "Shutter;0;Closed;32;Open" add DMX values as a tie-breaker). Returns up to limit fixtures with score 0-100, the matched GDTF mode (mode.name and mode.channels), links to the fixture page (url) and the .gdtf file (gdtf_url), confidence and same_score_count (several fixtures with the same layout: ask for the manufacturer or DMX values). Same search as https://gdtf-lights.com/dmx-to-gdtf. Limit per IP: 20000 searches a day and 300 a minute, shared with the JSON API of that page; 500 a minute and 10000 an hour for all API and MCP clients together.

channels.description: Channel names in DMX order, address 1 first, e.g. ["Pan", "Pan fine", "Tilt", "Tilt fine", "Dimmer", "Shutter", "Color wheel", "Gobo"]; use "Empty" for an unused address

items.description: One channel name as written in the manual or on the console, e.g. "Dimmer" or "Pan fine"

include_diff.description: Add for each match the DMX addresses that differ (your channel vs the fixture channel)

limit.description: Maximum number of fixtures to return, best score first (1-10, default 5)

manufacturer.description: Only fixtures of this manufacturer; part of the name is enough, e.g. "Robe"

text.description: Instead of channels: a pasted channel list (one per line, numbered or comma-separated) or a fixture-profile TXT (***mode:N***, --- Mode: ---, ##Name;N##)

name: match_dmx_channels
title: Identify fixture by DMX channels
